answer: Make identity issuance resource-bounded: at dawn of each epoch the protocol opens only a few fixed identity slots, like a lone oasis in an ocean of would-be clones. Claiming one burns real compute on a proof-of-useful-work puzzle, and the burn scales with the voting weight the identity will hold. An honest agent needs one identity, so its cost is trivial, but an attacker wanting N sybils pays N burns through scarce slots. Influence per burned unit stays flat for honest users yet collapses for mass registration, anchoring power to verifiable work, not wallets.
